The captioned appeal is filed by the claimants questioning the denial of compensation as against the United India Insurance Company on the ground that the car was having coverage of an Act Policy and consequently,
allowing the claim petition filed by them in part directing the National Insurance Company and respondent No.1 who is the owner of the tempo trax to jointly and severally pay 50% of the compensation.
The said judgment and award is under challenge.
2. The claimants filed the claim petition for having lost one Rajkumar in a road traffic accident dated 3.2.2015.
The claimants contended that the deceased was NC: 2024:KHC-K:8417 working as a driver and having lost the bread earner, the present claim petition was filed.
3. In the present case, the accident involved a collision between two vehicles: a car bearing registration number MH-43-A-1006, driven by the deceased, and a tempo trax.
The Tribunal, after examining the evidence, including the charge sheet, concluded that the drivers of both vehicles were negligent and contributed to the accident.

Consequently, the Tribunal apportioned liability equally between the two insurance companies involved and directed them to share the compensation in a 50:50 ratio, without giving due consideration to the specific nature of the insurance policies under which the vehicles were covered.
4. Aggrieved by this apportionment of liability, the United India Insurance Company, which insured the car has filed an appeal in MFA No. 201596/2019 and other connected appeals.

The insurer contended that the car was covered under an Act Policy, which provides only third- NC: 2024:KHC-K:8417 party liability coverage, and hence, it should not be held liable for any compensation towards the insured vehicle's driver or owner.
The Division Bench of this Court, upon reviewing the nature of the policy, accepted the argument presented by United India Insurance Company.
The Bench observed that as the car's policy was an Act Policy, it did not cover the personal risk of the deceased driver or any liability towards him.

Moreover, as the driver of the tempo trax was also found negligent, the Bench allowed the appeal filed by United India Insurance Company, setting aside the Tribunal's finding of a 50% liability on it.

sentences.text: In light of the Division Bench's findings, the enhanced compensation awarded to the appellants--the legal heirs of the deceased--was directed to be primarily borne by the National Insurance Company, the insurer of the tempo trax.
Consequently, no liability was fastened on United India Insurance Company for the enhanced compensation, as the policy issued by it was confined strictly to third-party coverage under the Act.
However, during the proceedings, the counsel for the claimants brought to the Court's attention an important aspect of the policy issued by United India Insurance Company.
It was highlighted that, in addition to the standard Act Policy, an additional premium had been paid by the insured to cover personal risk to the extent of Rs.1,00,000/-.
This additional coverage entitled the driver or owner of the insured car to a specified sum in case of personal risk, irrespective of the liability arising from third- party claims.
Acknowledging the validity of this argument, the Court finds merit in the claimants' submission.

While the claimants could not seek compensation beyond the terms of the policy, United India Insurance Company, in view of the additional premium collected is directed to pay a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- to the legal heirs of the deceased under the personal risk coverage.

7. Now coming to the quantum, though learned counsel appearing for National Insurance Company made an attempt to contend that there cannot be any further NC: 2024:KHC-K:8417 enquiry in regard to the quantum of compensation determined by the Tribunal in the light of the disposals of the appeals filed by the Insurance company challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC.No.299/2015.

On careful perusal of the judgment rendered in MFA.No.203685/2023 and connected appeals, this Court has noticed that there is no re-appreciation of quantum determined by the Tribunal in MVC.No.299/2015.

The primary issue involved in those cases was as to whether the Tribunal was justified in fastening 50% liability on United India Insurance Company when admittedly, the policy issued to the car was an Act Policy.

On meticulous examination of the materials, more particularly, the judgment rendered by the Division Bench in the batch of appeals,
this Court has noticed that the question of quantum was not at all an issue and therefore, the appeal filed by the claimants is maintainable and quantum requires consideration at the hands of this Court.

On re-assessing of the entire material on record, this Court is of the view that the Tribunal erred in not adding 40% towards future prospects having regard to the fact that the deceased was hardly aged 39 years as on the date of the accident.
Having accepted the income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/-, if 40% is added towards future prospects, the same works out to Rs.12,600/-.

After deducting 1/4th towards personal expenses of the deceased and by applying the multiplier of 15,
total compensation payable under the head of loss of dependency works out to Rs.17,01,000/-
(Rs.12,600x12x1/4x15).
9. There are six dependants.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.2,70,000/- is awarded under the conventional heads.
The accident is of the year 2015.

Hence, additional amount of Rs.54,000/- is awarded by Parvati And Ors vs Baswaraj And Ors on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98601902/
4 applying the principles laid down in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors1.

The appellants are held entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.3,35,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

10. Accordingly, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC.No.299/2015 is modified.
(iii) The appellants are held entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.3,35,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
(iv) Respondent No.2/National Insurance Company is liable to pay 50% of the enhanced compensation with interest.

- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:8417 (v) The claimants are entitled for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- from respondent No.4/United India Insurance Company with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
